changes.comment: BREAKING: a subscription records the principals that may bind and drain its delivery. ISubscribeRequest.drainPrincipals (non-empty, at most maxDrainPrincipals, de-duplicated and stored ascending) defaults to the registering principal alone, and the registrant is not added when a list is given; TaskBroker.bindDelivery refuses any other principal with not-found-or-denied, the answer a missing subscription gets, and so does TaskDeliveryPump.create. Every IBoundTaskDelivery operation applies the rule again to the subscription as it stands. Hosts that subscribe on an agent's behalf and let the agent drain must name the agent. A persisted subscription written without drain principals is drained by its registrant alone (drainPrincipalsOf; ITaskSubscription.drainPrincipals reports the rule applied). New TaskBroker.setSubscriptionDrain, through the registering principal's binding, replaces the drain principals and the recorded policy identity; a retry of the original subscribe after a change is conflict. BREAKING: IBoundTaskDelivery.disposeWithheld now requires the subscription to have recorded a policy identity (ISubscribeRequest.policyIdentity) and the binding's policy to carry the same one (new optional ITaskAuthorization.policyIdentity, read at binding; trustedKindAuthority takes it); it accepts any drain principal rather than only the registrant. A subscription without a recorded identity refuses every disposeWithheld. BREAKING (implementers only): ITaskRepositoryWriter gains setSubscriptionDrain.
